summary: One open-source delivery system runs the full assembly without a pull-request object. Mainstream platforms do not remove the review object, but merge queues, merge trains and policy engines can make machine gates the operative approval mechanism; the pull request may then remain as an automation envelope even when routine human diff approval is removed.

items.text: Agent Studio is the reference implementation: the platform owns every git operation as a pipeline step, publishes fenced delivery refs, runs a fail-closed build-and-test gate and named review aspects, integrates green deliveries into develop before human review, recomputes each card's integration state from attributed-commit ancestry, and refuses the completed state without either integration or an explicit, recorded operator override. A pull-request integration strategy remains configurable for repositories whose policy requires it.

GitHub merge queue validates required status checks against the latest target branch and queued changes before merge, then removes a failing entry. It replaces manual merge coordination with an integration-tested gate, although GitHub still uses a pull request as the queued change record.

GitLab merge trains create pipelines against the combined state of the target branch and earlier queued changes and merge only successful entries in order. This implements machine-validated integration and avoids a human having to re-evaluate stale branch state.

Mergify Merge Queue updates queued changes with their base, runs required CI and applies configurable queue rules before merging. It provides explicit policy, priorities and batch behavior for a gate-led delivery path.

SonarQube Quality Gates return a versioned pass/fail result over explicit analysis conditions and can block CI. They supply a deterministic quality standard that remains meaningful when routine human review is no longer mandatory.
